item_types.program: A program row taken from the agency's detailed "Appropriations, by Programs/Activities/Projects" table (FY2020 layout), or its summary "by Program" table where no detailed table is printed. amount = total as printed; total_derived_from_components marks rows where the Act prints no total.
item_types.sub_program: A sub-row nested under a program (e.g. a schools division, a hospital, a project). Sub-program amounts are already included in their parent program amount — do not add both.
item_types.infrastructure_project: One of the itemised Ministry of Public Works projects (capital outlay). Already included in the MPW "Road Network..." program amount.
item_types.special_provision: A numbered item in a section's Special Provisions. amount = the peso figure stated in the provision (earmark / ceiling), or null if none. These describe how program money is to be used and overlap with program rows — they are not additional appropriations.
item_types.special_provision_sub_item: A lettered or numbered sub-item under a special provision.

metadata.how_to_search: Filter line_items[] where tags contains the category (e.g. "Digitalization & ICT"), or use tag_index[category].item_ids. search_text holds the full text each item was matched on; free-text search on it also works.
metadata.tagging_method: Keyword/regex rules over the program path, agency/office name and (for provisions) the provision text, plus one sector tag inherited from the agency. Multiple tags per item are normal. Rules are listed in taxonomy[].keywords.

line_items.program_path: Quick Response Fund
line_items.name: Quick Response Fund
line_items.provision_text: Quick Response Fund. The amount appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for the replacement, reconstruction, rehabilitation or repair of school buildings and facilities in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occured in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occuring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and information initiatives, or any other authorized in this Act.

line_items.name: Engineering and Administrative Overhead Expenses The BARMM-MPW is authorized to deduct a m…
line_items.provision_text: Engineering and Administrative Overhead Expenses The BARMM-MPW is authorized to deduct a maximum of 3% from the appropriation of infrastructure projects to be used for the following: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals which shall be limited to those under job-orders or contracts of service or such other engagement of personnel without any employer- employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (iii) construction project management; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation and repair of heavy equipment, motor vehicles, laboratory apparatus, survey instruments and other related equipment and parts used in the implementation of infrastructure projects; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction activities: PROVIDED, That the engineering and administrative overhead expenses (EAO) shall be treated/booked-up as capitalized expenditures and shall form part of the project cost and that the EAO expenses shall not be authorized for infrastructure projects costing below One Million Pesos (P1,000,000). PROVIDED, FURTHER, that the acquisition of motor vehicles shall only be allowed when it is proven more economical than vehicle rental and that the acquisition thereof is consistent with the guidelines set forth in NBC 446 series of 1995, as amended by NBC 446-A series of 1998.
